checklist.notes: The final prompt asks “What did staff say?” although no staff reply appears in the story or dialogues, so the expected answer is not available in the supplied lesson.
The short station scenario, two request forms, three travel facts, and bounded recall remain manageable within 35 minutes at A2.1.

The lesson says Mai asked staff and later tests the staff response, but it models only Mai’s request and the Mai–Linh exchange; the missing staff turn breaks the request-to-mediation-to-listening chain.

The v4 blocker is resolved: contrasting staff and friend requests, contextual rationales, selection, adaptation, and an urgency exception now provide observable practice in socially suitable choice alongside narration and mediation.
The sequence moves from narrative recall to contextual request choice and adaptation, then mediation and pronunciation/listening review.
A learner cannot answer or self-check the required staff-speech question because the lesson supplies no staff utterance or answer key for it.
The explicit stress cue and concrete relationship-sensitive request contrast are supportive without making population-wide claims about Vietnamese learners.

findings.description: Section 4 requires the learner to report what staff said, and Section 3 claims Mai asked staff, but no staff response is present anywhere in the lesson. This makes one required listening/self-check item unanswerable and leaves the modeled mediation chain incomplete.
findings.recommendation: Within the existing authorized scope, add a brief staff response containing the relevant facts or change the final question and narrative claim so every required answer is explicitly available and checkable; do not add M7 exercises.
